title: Clarify embedding vector scaling and reranker scoring semantics
creator: Aisha Khan
description: We need to eliminate ambiguity in how the embeddings service and the reranker endpoint treat vector norms and distance metrics. Different model families produced by upstream tokenizers/encoders sometimes return non-unit vectors; downstream rerank logic has historically assumed normalized vectors for cosine, which has led to subtle ranking drift, inconsistent metrics between hosted and dedicated deployments, and customer confusion. This ticket defines a deterministic, backward-compatible approach that preserves existing customer results where possible, improves correctness for raw-dot use cases, and provides a migration path with monitoring and a lightweight detection shim.
acceptance_criteria: Reranker endpoint exposes an explicit scoring_mode parameter (values: "auto", "cosine", "dot") with clear semantics
Default behavior (auto) detects whether incoming embeddings are pre-normalized and chooses the metric without changing existing users' ranking results
Unit tests cover: pre-normalized inputs, raw (non-normalized) inputs, and mixed-batch cases
Benchmarks show p50/p95/p99 latency impact measured across small/medium/large batch sizes and on both hosted and dedicated configs
Migration docs and SDK examples published and linked; rollout plan executed with canary and automatic rollback on quality regression
technical_summary: We will implement three coordinated changes: (1) normalize-on-demand path inside reranker that only runs when scoring_mode=cose or when auto-detection finds non-unit vectors; (2) a detection heuristic that samples L2 norms in the batch and decides if normalization is necessary (fast path: compare to 1.0 within epsilon 1e-3); (3) a 'dot-with-scale' option to maintain exact legacy dot semantics when models intentionally produce length-encoded similarity. The implementation must avoid allocating large temporary buffers for normalization at high throughput; we will use mutable in-place normalization when the request owns the buffer and fall back to temp space for shared buffers.
benchmarks: Small batch (n=8, seq=1536) hosted: baseline p99=45ms, normalize-on-demand p99=48ms (+6.7%)
Medium batch (n=64) dedicated: baseline p99=120ms, normalize-on-demand p99=126ms (+5%)
Reranker accuracy (MS MARCO subset) after auto-detection: NDCG@10 change = +0.8% (improvement for mixed-norm models), when forcing dot-with-scale NDCG parity preserved with legacy behavior
implementation_plan: API: add scoring_mode field to rerank request schema and update OpenAPI spec and SDKs (python, go, node)
Runtime: implement in-place L2 norm sampler and normalization kernel in serving runtime so normalization cost is vectorized on GPU where available
Compatibility shim: server-side 'auto' runs quick norm sampling; if norms within [0.999,1.001] treat as normalized and skip heavy work
Tests: add deterministic golden fixtures for models that returned pre-normalized vectors historically and for raw outputs (include random seeds)
Docs: publish migration guide, changelog entry, and a sample script to validate old vs new scoring for customers
rollout_plan: Merge feature behind feature-flag and unexposed API default (auto remains current behavior until canary)
Dark launch: route 1% of traffic to new path and compare rankings + cost metrics in shadow mode for 72h
Canary: enable scoring_mode=auto for 5% of accounts and monitor NDCG/CTR regressions and p99 latency for 7 days
Full rollout: 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 2-3 weeks with automatic rollback if customer-impact metric breaches thresholds
monitoring_and_metrics: Add metric: rerank.norm_detected_rate (percent of requests normalized when scoring_mode=auto)
Quality metric: rerank.ndcg_change_by_model_family (baseline vs current) aggregated daily
Alert: if ndcg_change_by_model_family < -0.5% for >3h during canary, trigger rollback and paging
backwards_compatibility_notes: Default (auto) will attempt to preserve existing behavior by sampling incoming norms and skipping normalization if vectors are already unit-length within epsilon. For customers that relied on legacy length-encoded dot semantics, the scoring_mode="dot" (and dot_with_scale flag) will preserve exact legacy scores. We will include a one-week opt-in window where both old and new scoring are computed for each impacted request and diff logs stored in a transient S3 bucket to help customers verify parity.
